entries.title: Joshua 5:1
segments:
The sea; the Mediterranean. 
 
However much those who continue in sin may see of their own approaching ruin, they take no proper measures to escape it.

entries.title: Joshua 5:2
segments:
The second time; not that any who had been circumcised were to be circumcised again, but that the rite of circumcision, which had been neglected in the wilderness, was to be, as it were, established a second time as it had been the first time in Abraham's day. 
 
If under special and peculiar circumstances the ordinances of God have been for a time neglected, the earliest opportunity should be embraced to observe them, and thus to secure the benefits they are suited to impart.

entries.title: Joshua 5:3
segments: Whatever be the circumstances of men, it is safe, wise, and best for them to obey God.  He can protect them from all harm, or overrule what they may suffer for their highest good.

entries.title: Joshua 5:6
segments: By the dispensations of his providence, God fulfils the declarations of his word.

entries.title: Joshua 5:9
segments: The reproach of Egypt; according to some, the reproach of their having been bondmen in Egypt.  According to others, the reproach cast upon them by the Egyptians, as a race out of favor with God, and left by him to wander in the wilderness.  Compare

.  This reproach God had removed by receiving them again into covenant with himself by circumcision, and by giving them possession of the promised land. 
 
  Gilgal; that is, rolling away. 
 
Reproach may for a season rest upon the people of God, but in due time it shall be done away, and they shall be crowned with honor and glory.

entries.title: Joshua 5:10
segments: Fourteenth day; just forty years from the time of their keeping it on the evening before their departure from Egypt.

entries.title: Joshua 5:12
segments: When one source of support ceases, God opens another, and instead of leaving his people destitute, he will abundantly supply them with all real good.

entries.title: Joshua 5:13
segments: A man; One in the form and appearance of a man.  He was that "Angel of the Lord" who showed himself to be the Lord himself.

entries.title: Joshua 5:14
segments: Jehovah, who took the form of man, is the Captain of salvation to his people.  Those whom he saves worship him on earth, and will for ever worship him in heaven.
